summary: Gila NF Eagle Peak Lookout, Catron Co.: 1929 tower, 1955 CL-100 cab on a 10-ft base, NHLR-listed 2022, seasonal staff in 2020; probable duplicate of us-nm-eagle-peak.

facts.design: USDA Forest Service Standard Plan CL-100 to CL-106 series; 14 by 14 foot steel cab on a 10-foot base (the register says concrete blockhouse; another source says cinder block)

access.note: Active Forest Service fire lookout. The sources read do not say whether the cab is open to visitors; check with the Reserve Ranger District before going.

visit.trail_note: Reached by Wilson Canyon Trail #768 and Forest Road 38 (Eagle Peak Road). The Forest Service says the trail and road together are 1.5 miles one way. A road guide calls the summit road unpaved, with two sharp hairpin turns near its end.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Gila National Forest (Reserve Ranger District)

events.note: Earlier lookout tower on Eagle Peak, per Wikipedia and the Forest Lookouts page
CL-100 series cab on a 10-foot base replaced the 1929 tower; the register gives 1955 as the build year
A lookout was stationed on the peak as of April 15, with a second person about to join
Evaluated for the National Register under the Southwest lookouts theme; not eligible because of its age
Staffed by seasonal Forest Service employees, per the 2020 New Mexico chapter report
Registered May 22, 2022 as US 1586, NM 44; nominated by Mark Gutzman

corrections.why: The register gives the lookout at N 33.676873, W 108.576954 on the Reserve Ranger District, and Wikipedia places it about 18 miles east of Reserve. The current pair is about 0.7 degrees farther north. The us-nm-eagle-peak record already uses the register point.

corrections.proposed: no overall height until one is sourced
corrections.why: 3.0 m is about the 10-foot base, not the height of the tower. The register gives a 14x14 foot cab on a 10-foot concrete blockhouse base and no overall height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls the 10-foot base a concrete blockhouse. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a Forest Service history describing a 10-foot cinder block base that doubles as a storage room. The story reports both descriptions.

notes_for_editor: Probable duplicate of us-nm-eagle-peak: same tower, same county, same westlookouts source, same register entry. Merge or keep one. The story follows the same sources and reuses quotes already checked for the other id. This record's coordinates (34.38949, -108.68785) conflict with the register point; see corrections. The height_m of 3.0 looks like the 10-foot base.
